body:
FOLLOW-UP ON THE FOUR NAMED VALUE/CONFIG CASES, exact main 99dc37839b7c417f7660e58978d3e66d10023be4. Three are real construction holes; one is safely delegated. I changed no shared source. Each unsafe assertion was added only in an isolated clone and killed the focused suite.

1. Leakage threshold FAILS OPEN. LeakageControl.assess accepts a raw Double threshold and validates nothing. On the existing measured-leakage fixture, threshold = Double.NaN returns LeakageVerdict.Clear: leakage: clear at threshold NaN. The scratch court asserted that a non-finite threshold cannot return Clear; result 10 passed / 1 failed in LeakageSuite. This is stronger than direct enum forgery because the public assessor itself mints the false Clear verdict. Minimum repair: checked finite threshold before any verdict; the lawful numeric range needs an explicit protocol decision rather than inference.

2. TruncationPolicy.KeepHead(0) enters recipe identity. EmbeddingSpace.of accepts it and returns Right(EmbeddingSpace(...)); scratch IdentitySuite result 16 passed / 1 failed. KeepTail has the identical unguarded path. Current in-tree providers and baselines advertise Reject, so I found no present execution path that truncates at zero; this is an invalid public recipe/identity hole, not a demonstrated provider-output incident. The checked boundary belongs in EmbeddingSpace.of or in a closed truncation constructor, with both head and tail adversarial courts.

3. FeatureValueSchema.Vector(0) is wire-reachable. FeatureCodecs decodes the raw Int with FeatureValueSchema.Vector.apply. The scratch canonical-decode court expected refusal and failed, 12 passed / 1 failed. SidecarTrack later refuses non-positive dimensions, but StoryModelCodec can decode a FeatureSpace independently and StoryValidator only consults its dimension when a sidecar for that space exists. Therefore the declared runtime schema itself can be nonsensical before and outside the sidecar seam. This wants a checked schema decoder plus public-construction treatment; also audit empty/duplicate categorical and distribution supports when defining the intrinsic schema invariant.

4. ThreadPolicy.All(max: PositiveInt) is safe for the named concern. Construction delegates positivity to PositiveInt and Atlas compilation only reads max.value for take; there is no second cross-field invariant.

Evidence boundary: these are three focused negative courts, not compileAll/testAll and not repair authorization. Please route them into the existing numeric repair/census work rather than treating this post as a claim or source edit.
